s1.syndrome_frame: Acute cardiac syndrome with inflammatory and thrombotic features
salient_findings: Elevated cardiac markers (troponin and brain natriuretic peptide)
key_facts: 47-year-old man with no significant medical history
Exposure to COVID-19 through family member 12 days before death
Developed general malaise without fever or respiratory symptoms 2 days before death
Fatigue worsened over time, and patient was unable to eat the day before death
Patient was not vaccinated
Cardiopulmonary arrest occurred during transport to hospital
No coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis was observed
Elevated inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and IL-6)
SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive (>5000 pg/mL) from oropharyngeal swab
Postmortem CT scan showed dorsal pulmonary infiltrative shadow and bilateral pleural effusions
Pericardial effusion of 70 mL clear fluid
Heart weight was 426g, above normal range
Lung weights were above normal range

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated inflammatory cytokines and SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive, consistent with COVID-19 associated myocarditis

shortlist.label: COVID-19 associated pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Pericardial effusion and elevated inflammatory cytokines, consistent with COVID-19 associated pericarditis

shortlist.label: Fulminant myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse contraction band necrosis and lymphocytes in cardiac muscle, consistent with fulminant myocarditis

shortlist.label: Acute coronary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac markers and thrombocytopenia, although no coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis was observed

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Cardiopulmonary arrest and elevated cardiac markers, consistent with stress cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with cardiopulmonary arrest, elevated cardiac markers, and histology showing diffuse contraction band necrosis with lymphocytes in cardiac muscle, along with the absence of coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis, supports fulminant myocarditis, especially in the context of recent COVID-19 exposure and positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen test.

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: While myocarditis is a possible diagnosis, fulminant myocarditis better explains the severity and rapid progression of the patient's condition.

rejected.label: COVID-19 associated pericarditis
rejected.why: The presence of pericardial effusion could suggest pericarditis, but the primary issue seems to be myocardial, given the cardiac markers and histological findings.

rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
rejected.why: No coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis was observed, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's condition and the direct evidence of myocardial involvement point more towards an inflammatory cause like fulminant myocarditis rather than a stress-induced cardiomyopathy.

gold: COVID-19-related cardiac injury with diffuse myocardial necrosis
